Issued at 301 AM CDT Fri Sep 4 2026

An unusually strong late season mid-upper level ridge of high 
pressure continues to dominate the weather across much of the 
central and southern portions of the country east of the 
Rockies. Shortwave troughs rotating around the periphery of this
upper ridge continue to support MCS activity in a "ring of 
fire" type pattern more reminiscent of mid-summer than early 
September. 

One such shortwave is noted on water vapor imagery early this 
morning just north of International Falls. DCVA in advance of 
this shortwave combined with isentropic ascent associated with a
modest 25-30 kt low level jet has led to a couple of small 
MCSs. The one of most immediate concern locally is over central 
WI, near the nose of the west-southwesterly low level jet. An HP
supercell southwest of Green Bay has developed a bit of a cold 
pool and is showing signs of organizing into a small bowing 
convective line. Forward propagating Corfidi Vectors, 850-300 mb
thickness, and the instability gradient would all suggest this 
developing small bow should remain well north/northeast of our 
CWA. However, an outflow boundary from this line could 
accelerate down the lake and result in a wind shift to 
northeasterly across portions of northeast IL early this 
morning. This has been depicted to varying degrees by many CAM 
solutions over the past 24 hours. 

Absent any significant increase in the size and strength of the
attendant cold pool with the eastern WI MCS, it seems likely 
that the lake enhanced outflow should mix out by mid-late 
morning with winds turning southwesterly, even right up to the 
lakefront by early afternoon. This should set the stage for 
another day of unseasonably hot and humid conditions. Given 
925mb temps at near record levels in the mid-upper 20s Celcius, 
high temps solidly into the low to mid 90s appear likely today. 
Pooling dewpoints near and south of the synoptic warm front, 
enhanced by late season evapotranspiration should result in 
dewpoints in the 70s once again this afternoon. Peak afternoon 
heat indices of 100 to 107 degrees are likely this afternoon, 
with the typically higher dewpoint more agricultural areas 
likely seeing peak heat indices around 110 degrees again this 
afternoon. 

For this reason, have expanded the heat advisory north to 
encompass our entire CWA again today. Heat indices in Chicago 
failed to reach 100 degrees yesterday, so the 3+ consecutive day
100+ heat index criteria for an extreme heat warning for Cook 
County isn't going to be met. For our southern CWA, this will be
the 4th consecutive day with advisory level heat indices, which
could justify an upgrade to an excessive heat warning. However,
most nights have had low temperatures dipping into the lower 
70s with many hours of relief from the heat at night, so opted 
not to upgrade to an extreme heat warning for these areas. Given
the strong instability present and low level jet veering toward
the IL/WI border toward and just after sunrise, certainly 
cannot rule out the possibility of some isolated to widely 
scattered showers/storms developing near and behind the lake 
enhanced outflow boundary early this morning into northeast IL. 
However, forcing along this boundary is expected to be pretty 
shallow and low level jet likely to weaken diurnally, so threat 
of any isolated showers/storms should wrap up by mid-late 
morning. The remainder of today should be dry with no forcing 
mechanisms for any storms this afternoon. 

The upper ridge is expected to begin to retrograde westward 
tonight with mid-upper level height falls likely to allow a weak
cold front over the upper Great Lakes to begin moving 
southward. The trend in guidance has generally been toward a 
slower southward progression, which would make sense given the 
expectation of not much convection to our north to aid its 
southward push. There is still some signal in HREF guidance for 
some convection tonight ahead of this boundary, but with pretty 
muted forcing, opted to go with nothing more than 20-30% 
chances. 

If the progression of the front continues to slow in guidance, 
then it is probable that we will need to extend the heat 
advisory into Saturday for portions of our southern CWA. Given 
that confidence isn't all that high yet on frontal timing, opted
to defer any advisory extension for the day shift to consider. 
Behind the front, it will be somewhat cooler and a bit less 
humid, but probably still a bit above average for September. 
Temperatures and humidity will continue to moderate on Sunday. 

A period of moderately strong northerly winds down the full 
fetch of the lake should result in an increase in waves later 
Saturday through early Sunday. It is possible that a beach 
hazard statement may be needed for dangerous swim conditions for
a part of this weekend, which is the closing weekend of the 
beach season. 

Dry and seasonably warm weather is expected Labor Day.
